title: Ops micro-worker: on-demand admin utilities + stepwise runbook taskization
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Goal: ship a lightweight 'ops micro-worker' that can execute single-step admin utilities and a stepwise taskization layer to convert canonical runbook steps into discrete, observable tasks. Background: multiple incidents showed friction when engineers needed to run ad-hoc admin commands (DB compact, cache purge, KV repair) without a safe, audited surface. The micro-worker should: 1) accept typed step manifests, 2) run in a constrained sandbox with permission lookup, 3) emit structured telemetry for each step, and 4) support dry-run + idempotency checks. Acceptance criteria: a) worker binary + library published, b) 3 canonical runbook steps packaged as task manifests and executed end-to-end in staging, c) per-step tracing in Console traces and token-cost telemetry surfaced, d) gating: feature flag + RBAC check before prod rollout. Non-goals: not building a full workflow engine or replacing long lived runbook orchestration; the micro-worker focuses on short, human-triggered remediations. Design notes: use existing admin-runtime RPC surface, add an adapters layer for 'shelllet' vs 'api-call' vs 'scripted' step types, enforce execution timeouts and retry budget. Telemetry: emit event types step.started, step.completed, step.failed, step.dryrun, with tags (caller, env, runbook_id, step_id, duration_ms). Safety: require KMS-signed manifests for sensitive actions, integrate with guardrail service to block unsafe param patterns. Rollout plan: internal dogfood on staging (1 week), limited production pilot for SRE on canary cluster (2 weeks), then org-wide opt-in. Links: PR skeleton https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-microworker/pull/1, design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ops+Microworker+Spec, preliminary eval dashboard https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ops-microworker-staging. Trade-offs: choosing a small dedicated worker reduces blast radius but increases operational surface (more binaries to manage). If timeboxed, we will scope to two step types (api-call, command-wrapper) and expand adapters post-MVP. Metrics to track: mean step latency, success rate, number of blocked safety checks, dry-run vs live ratio, and audit log volume.
